topic: Why regional sub-dialects like Sambalpuri and Cuttacki deserve distinct treatment on screen rather than being merged into a generic dialect
caption:
If you make a character from Sambalpur speak the exact same flat, standardized Odia as someone from Cuttack, you aren’t just being lazy with the writing—you’re flattening the map.

The sharp sass in Cuttacki street slang and the heavy, rhythmic warmth of Sambalpuri carry entirely different worldviews, not just different pronunciations.

When we force a generic, "neutral" dialect on screen to make it easy, we lose the humor, the grit, and the texture of how people actually live. 

Audiences don't need things watered down; they want to hear the truth of the soil.
